title: Development of a Dual Laser Phase Plate at CZII
content: A laser phase plate (LPP), in which a phase shift of unscattered electrons is introduced via interaction of electrons with strong laser fields [1], has been shown to significantly increase contrast in cryo electron microscopy [2]. This new approach has demonstrated the possibility of accurate control of the phase shift value for prolonged periods of time [4]. However, certain properties of a single LPP may require further improvement. Particularly, the presence of ghost images, which are the result of diffraction of the electron beam on the standing laser wave, may deteriorate the image quality and require complicated image processing algorithms for removal. The high laser power required to operate the SLPP also imposes limitations on the quality of the cavity mirrors and leads to thermally induced deformations of the mirrors, further complicating the operation of the optical cavity.
